title: fix(claim): release the contested claim on walk-away and let staleness clear disputes
body:
## Background

A lost two-way claim race currently locks an issue against all
mechanical reclaim, contradicting the documented promise that "the
24 h stale-takeover … remain[s] the race-recovery backstop"
(`idd-claim.instructions.md`).

Two halves combine into the livelock:

1. **Instruction side.** `idd-claim.instructions.md`'s Claim
   verification "If any check fails" paragraph (after the 5 checks)
   directs: treat the claim as contested, return to Discover, do not
   retry the same issue — with no instruction to post `unclaimed-by`.
   The lite mirror is stricter still: "Any failure → claim contested
   → STOP, do not proceed". When sessions A and B race through the
   documented A5 TOCTOU window a few seconds apart, A's step 4 sees
   B's strictly-later marker (contested → walk away) and B's step 3
   sees A active (walk away). Neither posts a release, so A's claim
   stays active with no live owner.
2. **Helper side.** In `src/scripts/resume-claim-routing.mts`, the
   route decision checks `laterCompetingClaim` **before**
   `isStaleByAge`, so once a later competing claim exists the
   `--fresh-claim-gate` returns `disputed`/`already-claimed` forever —
   including after the active claim passes the 24 h staleness bound.
   Discover Step 1.5's recommended mechanical path is exactly this
   helper (`resume-claim-routing.mjs --fresh-claim-gate`), so via the
   documented path the issue stays ineligible **indefinitely**, not
   merely for `claim-stale-age`.
   `findLaterCompetingClaim` also scans raw `claimed-by` markers and
   never reconciles a competitor's own `unclaimed-by` release, so even
   a courteous loser that releases its raced claim does not clear the
   dispute.

Same-second races self-heal via the tie-break; only different-second
races livelock. The owner-resume `disputed`/`stop` behavior is
test-locked (`tests/resume-claim-routing.test.mts`) and appears
intended; the missing staleness escape and missing release are the
defects.

## Proposed change

1. In `resume-claim-routing.mts`, evaluate staleness of the *active*
   claim before (or combined with) the `laterCompetingClaim` branch,
   so a stale disputed claim still routes to `stale`/`takeover` for a
   fresh session. Keep the owner-resume dispute semantics unchanged.
2. Reconcile competitor releases: a competing `claimed-by` whose
   claim-id has a later matching trusted `unclaimed-by` no longer
   counts as a live competitor in `findLaterCompetingClaim`.
3. In `idd-claim.instructions.md` step 4 (and the lite mirror,
   `lite/idd-claim-lite.instructions.md`), instruct the abandoning
   session that verified itself as the *parsed winner* to post
   `unclaimed-by` for its own `{claim-id}` before returning to
   Discover — it provably owns the active claim, so the release is
   safe and restores the issue to unclaimed.
4. Mirror the instruction edits into `idd-template/` sources and keep
   the enforced bundle byte budgets passing.
5. Add unit tests: (a) stale + disputed → `takeover`; (b) released
   competitor no longer yields `disputed`; (c) existing owner-resume
   dispute cases unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--fresh-claim-gate` on an issue whose active claim is older
      than `claim-stale-age` returns a takeover-eligible route even
      when a later competing claim marker exists.
- [ ] A competitor claim followed by its own trusted `unclaimed-by`
      does not produce `disputed`.
- [ ] Claim verification step 4 (full + lite + template mirrors)
      instructs the losing-but-active winner to release before
      walking away.
- [ ] Existing `resume-claim-routing` tests still pass; new tests
      cover the two new behaviors; `pnpm test` passes.
- [ ] `node scripts/idd-doctor.mjs` (bundle byte audit) passes after
      the instruction edits.
- [ ] Generated `scripts/*.mjs` matches `pnpm run build` output.

Refs: 2026-07-28 fresh-model audit (helper + corpus agents converged
on this defect independently); adjacent open design question #1529
(activation-nonce cold recovery) is unaffected.
